quā^drīni , ae, a,
I.num. distrib. adj. [quattuor], four each, four (ante-class. and postAug.): “ab uno uni, a tribus trini, a quattuor quadrini,” Varr. L. L. 8, § 55 Müll.: si haberem quadrinas molas, Pompon. ap. Non. 483, 24: “dies,” Plin. 11, 36, 43, § 120 : “febris quadrini circuitūs,” a quartan fever, id. 7, 50, 51, § 170 : “cardines,” Arn. 6, 192 : “temporum vices,” App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 7, 16 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
